title: GPU retimer oscillation triage cheatsheet (on-call synthesis)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight on-call reference for triaging a specific failure mode we started seeing in late 2026: short, repeating NVLink/PCIe link flaps tied to retimer oscillation that often precede ECC bursts and occasional kernel panics. The doc captures immediate signals, first-response commands, safe mitigations, and investigative next steps.

Summary (one-liner):
Transient retimer oscillation -> momentary link retrain -> ECC correctable-error spike -> driver context loss -> possible kernel panic. Affected nodes show repeated NVLink retrain events and fast oscillations in link properties rather than a stable long-duration failure.

Impact profile:
- A subset of jobs (long-context decode and KV-cache heavy workloads) see degraded throughput or OOMs when GPU context is lost.
- Short-duration errors often auto-recover; repeated oscillations cause job restarts and can cascade into scheduler churn.
- Historically 1–3 nodes/day at scale; reproducible in lab with stressed retimer firmware on one HW revision.

When to use this doc (triggers):
- Pager: GPU-Node-ECC-Spike or NVLINK-Retrain spiking alerts.
- Symptoms: multiple soft ECC increases within minutes, nvidia-driver lost context, repeated mdmesg lines with nvlink or pcie retrain.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Isolate node: mark node unschedulable in k8s (cordon) and stop new jobs.
   - kubectl cordon <node> ; kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node> (if immediate evac needed).
2) Collect quick telemetry (attach to incident Slack thread):
   - nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERF,FB,POWER,TEMPERATURE
   - nvidia-smi topo -m
   - nvidia-smi -a | egrep -i "ecc|error|link|retimer|nvlink" -A4
   - dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200 | egrep -i "nvlink|nvrm|NVRM|GPU|ecc|ERR|panic|tainted" -n
   - journalctl -k -u nvidia-* --no-pager --since "15 minutes ago" | sed -n '1,200p'
3) Determine if topology change or retrain noise present:
   - Check nvlink retrain messages: dmesg lines usually include "nvlink: retrain" or "link retrain". Count frequency.
4) Snapshot metrics: GPU temps, power, ECC counts, retimer temperature if available, PCIe link width/speed (lspci -vvv).

Immediate safe mitigations (choose based on risk):
- If single node and flapping: Drain then reboot (soft reboot) to clear retimer state: sudo systemctl reboot.
- If cluster-wide correlated: Enable auto-fallback to alternate region/model pool (routing) and increase capacity from Dedicated burst if configured.
- If job is critical and intermittent: restart just the pod on a different node (reschedule).
- Avoid firmware reflash or power-cycle in first 15 minutes unless confirmed hardware cause.

Commands and log snippets to collect (full forensic set):
- nvidia-smi -q -d ALL > /tmp/nvidia-smi-all-$(date +%s).txt
- dmesg --ctime > /tmp/dmesg-$(date +%s).txt
- journalctl -u kubelet -u docker --since "1 hour ago" > /tmp/kube-docker-log.txt
- lspci -vvv | egrep -A4 "3d|VGA|NVIDIA" > /tmp/lspci.txt
- python3 -c 'import subprocess, json,sys;print(subprocess.check_output(["/usr/bin/nvidia-smi","-q","-x"]).decode())' > /tmp/nvidia-xml-$(date +%s).xml
- collect nvlink counters (if driver supports): cat /sys/class/drm/card*/nvlink_status* (path varies by kernel/driver).
- gpu telemetry: curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | egrep "gpu.*temp|gpu.*ecc|gpu.*power" > /tmp/metrics-$(date +%s).txt

Important signals that indicate hardware retimer problem vs. transient noise:
- Hardware-retimer signature: deterministic retrain patterns tied to retimer HW errors in dmesg, retrain cadence consistent across reboots, retimer temp anomalies in BMC sensors.
- Transient: single retrain, ECC count increments but no PCIe link width downshift, jobs recover after restart.

Runbook draft (step-by-step):
1) Contain: cordon/drain node. Capture logs above. Notify scheduler and customer impact if any jobs evicted.
2) Non-disruptive remediation: soft reboot and re-verify. If errors stop, keep node cordoned for 4 hours and monitor ECC and retrain counters.
3) If persists after reboot: power-cycle at rack PDU (coordinate with oncall ops) and capture BMC logs surrounding power event.
4) If still persists: escalate to hardware team for retimer firmware introspection; propose moving node to maintenance and swapping to spare board.
5) Post-incident: record node serial, HW revision, firmware versions (GPU, retimer), PDU history, ambient temp; open hardware ticket (IR-6621-like) and attach artifacts.

Automated detection heuristic (proposed):
- Alert when: >3 retrain events across any GPU on a node within 10 minutes AND ECC correctable-errors increase by >50 within same window.
- Action: auto-cordon node + start log-collection job. Pager to SRE.

Suggested alert thresholds (tunable):
- Soft ECC surge: 50 correctables / 10 min -> warning.
- NVLink retrain: 3 retrains / 10 min -> warning.
- Combined (above both true) -> P1.

Observations from lab repro (notes):
- Stressing retimer with continuous link retrain tool causes a deterministic ECC burst on adjacent GPUs after ~7–10 minutes.
- Some HW revisions show mitigation when retimer firmware is pinned to v1.3.2; newer revisions regress under certain voltage profiles.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Inventory: which host HW revisions have retimer v1.3.x vs v1.4.x? (owner: Ethan)
- Can we add retimer temperature telemetry to exporter? (owner: Sofia)
- Should scheduler avoid mixing retimer-revision nodes in same rack? (owner: Liam)

Postmortem checklist (if this becomes a major incident):
- Timeline of retrain/ECC increases with UTC timestamps.
- Job manifests and logs for affected workloads.
- Node hardware metadata and firmware images.
- Compare with historical incident IR-4512 and IR-5310 (attach).

Notes to on-call: keep conservatism over haste. Retimer oscillation can look like software driver bugs (nvidia module) but frequently is hardware/firmware. Collect full artefacts before attempting destructive fixes. If you must swap hardware, ensure you tag components and record serial numbers.

Appendix: useful references
- Confluence: GPU Retimer Diagnostics (linked above).
- Kernel logging patterns: sample dmesg lines to watch for ("nvlink: lane retrain", "NVRM: Xid", "nvidia: GPU XXX lost context").
- Infra PR: automated node-cordon-on-ecchigh (draft) in repo link above.

This doc is a pragmatic synthesis of multiple on-call notes; use it as a checklist and keep it updated with lab data. After next maintenance window we'll convert high-confidence remediation steps into a formal runbook and add automated playbooks for collection and cordon actions.
